Eleni: quick one from the canary yesterday - partial tenant swaps left ~20% of a customer's traffic hitting old region. we need clear rollback semantics and an idempotent abort path.
Rajat: what happened exactly?
Eleni: when batch B2 aborted midway we stopped prewarm for remaining tenants but didn't retract DNS/edge routing for those already moved. logs: ```[7191112224] swap-start batch=B2 tenant=acct-77
[7191112226] swap-complete tenant=acct-77 -> target=eu-west-1
[7191112228] swap-abort batch=B2 reason=prewarm-timeout
[7191112229] traffic-split tenant=acct-77 old=23% new=77%
```
Marta: oof. rollback semantics must be explicit: noop, revert, or finalize. default should be revert for non-resident low-write, finalize for resident-locked only after manual sign-off.
Tomas: implementation note: reversion has two parts: (1) control-plane: cancel batch and issue revert job, (2) data-plane: instruct edge-proxies to shift weights with a smooth ramp over 30s and invalidate partial prewarm caches in target region. make revert idempotent.
Rajat: API: `POST /v1/swap-batches/{id}/abort?mode=revert|finalize|noop` and `POST /v1/swap-batches/{id}/revert` should be safe to call multiple times. emit `swap.batch.revert.started|succeeded|failed`.
Eleni: also add a safety check: disallow revert if legal-resident tenant already has writes in new region unless legal-approved. surface as `abort_blocked=legal_residency`.
Marta: telemetry: `swap.partial.count`, `swap.revert.latency`, `swap.traffic.ramp` so SRE can tune ramp windows.
ops-bot: :rotating_light: swap-batch B2 aborted at 7191112228 (reason=prewarm-timeout)
Tomas: tests: create batch, simulate prewarm timeout mid-batch, assert repeated `revert` calls leave tenant routing identical to pre-batch state and no duplicate model loads.
Eleni: thanks all - i'll add a compact RFC appendix with API wire shapes and a short runbook snippet for operators. ping for review when done.
